userStories.title: Fleet read-model must exclude the roster-hidden agents (per-workspace Auto + ephemeral clones)
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (chain 5/6 adversarial review). The fleet agents query filters by workspace only — services/fleet_state.py:380-381 `db.query(Agent).filter(Agent.workspace_id == workspace_id)` — so it returns EVERY agent in the workspace, including the two categories the canonical roster deliberately hides: (a) the per-workspace system agent Auto (is_system_agent=True, workspace_id set) — core/seeds/seed_auto_agent.py:15 documents it as 'hidden from the Roster UI (is_system_agent=True + workspace_id != None)', and it is seeded into every provisioned workspace, so it appears on EVERY fleet response; and (b) ephemeral Mission Zero clones (agent_type='ephemeral') — services/coordinator_service.py:585 'hidden from roster, cleaned up after mission', present during any onboarding run. The canonical roster excludes both: api/agents.py:538 `.filter(Agent.agent_type != "ephemeral")` and api/agents.py:545-547 `~and_(Agent.is_system_agent.is_(True), Agent.workspace_id.isnot(None))`. Consequence: the fleet TAB and the roster TAB on the SAME Agents page show different agent sets; platform_fleet_status lists Auto (the very agent asking 'how's the team doing?') as a team member, plus onboarding clones during Mission Zero — directly undermining PRD-228 goals G2/G3 (a grounded, accurate 'what's everyone doing' answer). The service docstring (fleet_state.py:369 '1. active agents in the workspace') MISDESCRIBES the actual behavior. Untested: the realdb fixture (tests/test_prd228_fleet_state_realdb.py:74-85) seeds only agent_type='custom' agents with no Auto/ephemeral, so no test exercises the real agent population. Global system agents/templates (workspace_id=None) are already excluded by the workspace filter — the delta is exactly {per-workspace Auto} + {ephemeral clones}. FIX: mirror the roster's exclusions in the agents query and correct the docstring; if including Auto is a deliberate product choice it must be made explicit, but the default must match the roster.
acceptanceCriteria: The get_fleet_state agents query (services/fleet_state.py:380-384) excludes ephemeral agents (`Agent.agent_type != "ephemeral"`) AND the per-workspace system agent (`~and_(Agent.is_system_agent.is_(True), Agent.workspace_id.isnot(None))`), mirroring api/agents.py:538 and :545-547 — one query, still workspace-scoped, still no N+1 DONE — fleet_state.py agents query gained both predicates in one .filter() (single query, workspace-scoped); `and_` added to the sqlalchemy import. Both Agent columns are NOT NULL (agent_type nullable=False; is_system_agent server_default='false') so `!=`/is_() have no NULL-filter surprise. userStories.title: Route must fail-soft on the omittable enrichment sources (watches/asks), not 500
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (chain 5/6 adversarial review). The binding rule (prd-228.json line 4) is 'fail-soft per source (an unavailable source omits its fields, never 500s — clone the channels sender posture)'; PRD-228 §7 'tolerate partial sources ... by omitting fields, not failing'. Only the COST source is wrapped: services/fleet_state.py:162-181 `_safe_cost` (used at :436). The other two independently-omittable enrichment sources — watches (services/fleet_state.py:413-420) and asks (services/fleet_state.py:422-430) — are UNWRAPPED, so if either query raises (a schema drift / lock / bad row on `watches` or `approval_grants`; cf. the escalation_level migration-drift class already seen in this codebase), the exception propagates out of get_fleet_state and the route (api/fleet.py:36-42, which has no try/except) returns 500. The tool path is protected (handlers_fleet.py:138-142 returns {success:false}) but the ROUTE is not, so a single enrichment-source failure blanks the entire fleet tab ('Fleet state failed to load') even though agents/board/current-work/cost are all healthy — the opposite of the intended degrade-and-omit posture. NOTE: watches/blocked are NON-optional in the frontend contract (FleetAgentRow in api-client.ts), so the correct degrade is to DEFAULT these fields (watches → {active:0, needs_attention:0}; blocked.open_asks → []) rather than drop the keys, keeping the response shape-complete. The core sources (agents/board/mission) are structural and out of scope — they may still raise.
acceptanceCriteria: The watches source and the asks source in get_fleet_state degrade fail-soft (wrapped like `_safe_cost`): a failure of either is caught, logged, and yields safe defaults (watches → {active:0, needs_attention:0}; blocked → {count from board only, open_asks: []}) with all agents and cost/current intact — get_fleet_state does not raise DONE — fleet_state.py isolates each enrichment query (`_watches_source`/`_asks_source`) behind a fail-soft wrapper (`_safe_watches`/`_safe_asks`, services/fleet_state.py:211-256): try → return rows; except → logger.warning(exc_info=True) + return None. get_fleet_state calls the wrappers (:527-528). `_assemble_fleet` reads None as source-failed and defaults kept-not-dropped fields: watches → {active:0, needs_attention:0}, blocked.open_asks → [] (blocked.count still from the board source); cost keeps its existing `_safe_cost` posture. Read-only invariant intact (no .add/.commit/.flush in the service).

New test: monkeypatch the watches query to raise → get_fleet_state returns a whole 200-shaped response (every agent present, cost_24h + current intact, watches defaulted); same for the asks query DONE — test_prd228_fleet_state.py: test_get_fleet_state_failsoft_watches_still_200_shaped (monkeypatch _watches_source raises → 2 agents present, cost_available True, current+cost intact, watches=={active:0,needs_attention:0}) + test_get_fleet_state_failsoft_asks_still_200_shaped (blocked.open_asks==[]) + test_safe_watches_and_safe_asks_return_none_on_failure + test_assembler_defaults_when_watches_or_asks_unavailable (watches=None/asks=None → defaults; blocked.count still 1 from board). get_fleet_state does not raise.

Route-level test: GET /api/v1/fleet returns 200 (not 500) when a non-cost enrichment source fails (extend tests/test_prd228_fleet_route.py or the realdb suite) DONE — test_prd228_fleet_route.py::test_route_returns_200_when_enrichment_source_fails drives the REAL read-model (get_fleet_state not stubbed) through _RealishSession with _watches_source monkeypatched to raise → resp.status_code==200 (not 500), body.agents present, watches defaulted to {active:0,needs_attention:0}.

userStories.title: Fleet 'mirrors the roster exactly' is false for admin/super_admin viewers (global system agents like Auto CTO appear in the Roster tab, never in the Fleet tab)
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (chain 5/6 adversarial re-review). The RVW-1 fix documents the fleet population as 'mirrors the canonical roster exactly (api/agents.py) ... So the fleet TAB and the roster TAB on the same Agents page show the same set' (services/fleet_state.py:9-14 module docstring) and the entry-point comment '1. the workspace's roster agents ... mirroring api/agents.py's roster exclusions' (services/fleet_state.py:466-468). That contract is FALSE for admin/super_admin callers. api/agents.py list_tasks/list_agents builds scope as `workspace_predicate OR system_predicate` for admin/super_admin roles (api/agents.py:518-532): system_predicate = `and_(Agent.is_system_agent.is_(True), Agent.status == 'active', or_(Agent.required_role.is_(None), Agent.required_role.in_(visible_roles)))` (api/agents.py:525-530). It then excludes only ephemeral (api/agents.py:538) and the PER-WORKSPACE system agent (api/agents.py:545-547 `~and_(is_system_agent, workspace_id.isnot(None))`). A GLOBAL system agent (workspace_id=None) matches system_predicate and is NOT excluded by that per-workspace filter, so it stays in the roster for admins. Such a row is live and non-vestigial: core/seeds/seed_cto_agent.py:94-101 seeds 'Auto CTO' with workspace_id=None, is_system_agent=True, required_role='admin', status='active' (wired across api/agent_endpoints.py, api/chat.py, api/wizard.py, consumers/chatbot/service.py). The fleet agents query (services/fleet_state.py:477-496) filters `Agent.workspace_id == workspace_id`, which can NEVER match workspace_id=None, so Auto CTO never appears in the fleet. Consequence: an admin's Roster tab lists Auto CTO; the same admin's Fleet tab (and platform_fleet_status) omit it — the tabs show different sets and the docstring's 'exactly / same set' claim is untrue for every admin in every workspace. Untested: the realdb roster-mix fixture (tests/test_prd228_fleet_state_realdb.py:248-271) seeds only a PER-WORKSPACE Auto (workspace_id set), never a global system agent, so no test exercises the admin divergence. NOTE ON THE FIX: a workspace_id=None global persona carries no per-workspace floor state (no workspace-scoped board/mission/cost), so listing it in a per-workspace read-model would be permanently-idle noise — the correct default resolution is to make the docstring + comment HONEST about the real scope (the fleet shows the workspace's OWN roster agents, and intentionally excludes the global platform system agents the roster surfaces to admins), NOT to thread the caller role into the service. If admin parity IS the desired product behaviour, that is Gerard's call — surface it, do not choose it silently.
acceptanceCriteria: The services/fleet_state.py module docstring (:9-14) and the entry-point comment (:466-468) no longer state the fleet 'mirrors the canonical roster exactly' or that the two tabs 'show the same set' unconditionally; they state the exact scope (the workspace's own roster agents — non-ephemeral, non-per-workspace-system) AND explicitly note that GLOBAL platform system agents (workspace_id=None, e.g. Auto CTO) which api/agents.py surfaces to admin/super_admin roles are intentionally excluded because they carry no per-workspace floor state DONE — fleet_state.py module docstring rewritten (:9-24): drops 'mirrors the canonical roster exactly' / 'show the same set'; states the exact scope (workspace's OWN roster agents — non-ephemeral, non-per-workspace-system) + documents that GLOBAL system agents (workspace_id=None, e.g. Auto CTO via seed_cto_agent.py) which api/agents.py surfaces to admin/super_admin are intentionally omitted (no per-workspace floor state). Entry-point comment #1 and the inline filter comment updated to match.

New test documenting the intended behaviour: an agent with is_system_agent=True + workspace_id=None + required_role='admin' + status='active' is ABSENT from get_fleet_state for any workspace (pure structural against the query, or a realdb case extending the roster_mix fixture with a global system agent). The test names the divergence from api/agents.py's admin roster so a future reader knows it is intended, not an oversight [orchestrator/tests/] DONE — realdb behavioural proof tests/test_prd228_fleet_state_realdb.py::test_global_system_agent_absent_from_fleet (global_system_mix seeds a normal agent + a GLOBAL Auto CTO row: is_system_agent=True/workspace_id=None/required_role='admin'/status='active' → get_fleet_state returns ONLY the normal agent; the global id is absent), naming the api/agents.py:525-530 admin-roster divergence as intentional. Local doc-guard tests/test_prd228_fleet_state.py::test_agent_population_docstring_is_honest_about_admin_global_system_agents asserts the false 'exactly'/'same set' claims are gone + the divergence is documented.

If admin parity (including the global system agent in the fleet) is chosen instead of the doc correction, the choice is raised as an open question in the PR body for Gerard — never silently implemented by threading role into the service DONE — resolution = the RVW-3 DEFAULT (doc correction). That is proven ONLY for the open-full fallback: tests/test_prd228_fleet_tool.py:215-225 (test_visible_in_heartbeat_dispatcher_surface) calls `registry.to_dispatcher_schema(exclude_admin=True, allowed_names=None)` — its OWN comment concedes this 'mirrors the default open-full fallback the heartbeat tick uses when no query narrows the enum.' But the PRODUCTION heartbeat tick ALWAYS supplies a query: services/heartbeat_service.py:743-752 passes `query=task_description` with the comment 'Narrow the dispatcher enum to heartbeat-relevant actions — without a query this lane shipped all 137 on every run.' HEARTBEAT_ORCHESTRATOR uses tool_loading='dispatcher_only' (modules/context/modes.py:66-74); _load_dispatcher_only(query) (modules/context/sections/tools.py:129-155) calls _narrow_dispatcher_actions_async(query, ...) which, when SEMANTIC_TOOL_ROUTING is on and the query is non-empty (modules/tools/tool_router.py:266-280 → _narrow_dispatcher_actions_async_inputs returns None → ranking runs), calls _rank_actions_for_dispatcher_async(query, top_k=15, exclude_promoted=True). SEMANTIC_TOOL_ROUTING defaults true and SEMANTIC_TOOL_ROUTING_TOP_K defaults 15 (config.py:963-964) against ~138 registered actions. So on every real tick the dispatcher enum is the semantic top-15; platform_fleet_status (modules/tools/discovery/actions_fleet.py — not promoted, and exclude_promoted=True would drop it from ranking even if it were) has NO guaranteed slot and no page-prior (the heartbeat agent has no page manifest). If it does not rank top-15 for the health-check query on a given tick, the standing loop never sees the tool and PRD-228 §5 Component C / G2 ('the standing loop can flag anomalies proactively') silently does not happen — the documented signal-tool-routing-drop failure class (memory: architecture-signal-tool-routing-pitfall — native tools dropped by router narrowing when not in an always-included set). The AC's test gives false confidence because it exercises the allowed_names=None path production never runs (only reached on ranking failure/timeout/flag-off, not the happy path).
acceptanceCriteria: A test exercises the SAME query-narrowed dispatcher path the heartbeat runs (SEMANTIC_TOOL_ROUTING on, a representative non-empty heartbeat query threaded through _load_dispatcher_only / _narrow_dispatcher_actions_async), and asserts platform_fleet_status is reachable in the resulting dispatcher enum — not merely present in the registry or in the allowed_names=None open-full schema [orchestrator/tests/] DONE — tests/test_prd228_fleet_tool.py::test_heartbeat_dispatcher_always_includes_fleet_under_semantic_narrowing drives the SAME loader the heartbeat runs (ToolsSection().load_tools(strategy=DISPATCHER_ONLY, query='Perform a scheduled health check…')) with _narrow_dispatcher_actions_async monkeypatched to return a DECIDED narrowed top-K that omits platform_fleet_status (as if it ranked #16+), and asserts platform_fleet_status IS in the resulting dispatcher enum — via the always-include union, not the allowed_names=None open-full path (assert 'platform_fleet_status' not in the ranked list; assert it in the final enum; a non-promoted ranked entry preserved).

platform_fleet_status is reachable on a heartbeat tick REGARDLESS of ranking outcome (e.g. it is added to the heartbeat's guaranteed/always-include set for the dispatcher_only surface, or otherwise pinned for HEARTBEAT_ORCHESTRATOR) — reachability must not depend on an unasserted semantic-ranking result; the mechanism chosen follows the existing always-include/promotion pattern (no os.getenv outside config.py, no new tables) DONE — mechanism = a guaranteed always-include set for the dispatcher_only surface (dispatcher_only is used ONLY by HEARTBEAT_ORCHESTRATOR, modes.py:66-71, so this is heartbeat-scoped). config.HEARTBEAT_DISPATCHER_ALWAYS_INCLUDE (CSV, default 'platform_fleet_status'; os.getenv only in config.py, mirrors TOOL_FALLBACK_PINS) → tool_router._apply_dispatcher_always_include unions the pins onto any NARROWED allow-list (open-full/None left untouched — full enum already exposes it), each pin cleared by _page_action_passes_gate (same fail-closed gate page-prior uses → a gated/unknown pin is never forced in). Called from _load_dispatcher_only after _narrow_dispatcher_actions_async, so reachability no longer depends on the ranking result. No new tables. Unit tests: _apply…_unions_onto_narrowed_but_not_openfull, _drops_unknown_or_gated_pin, _defaults_to_fleet_status.

The existing test_visible_in_heartbeat_dispatcher_surface (tests/test_prd228_fleet_tool.py:215-225) is updated or supplemented so it no longer claims to prove heartbeat visibility using only allowed_names=None; the narrowed production path is what the AC verifies DONE — the old test_visible_in_heartbeat_dispatcher_surface is renamed to test_visible_in_heartbeat_dispatcher_surface_openfull_fallback with a docstring stating it covers ONLY the open-full FALLBACK (flag off / no query / rank failure → allowed_names=None), that this does NOT prove production visibility, and pointing to test_heartbeat_dispatcher_always_includes_fleet_under_semantic_narrowing (the narrowed production path + always-include union) as the P228-RVW-4 proof.

userStories.title: blocked.count is computed but surfaced by NO consumer — an approval-/manually-blocked agent renders 'idle' in the fleet tab and platform_fleet_status, so 'is anyone stuck?' misses it
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (chain 5/6 adversarial re-review). The read-model computes blocked.count from blocked_at (services/fleet_state.py:373 `blocked_count = sum(1 for t in my_board if t.blocked_at is not None)`; emitted at :409 `"blocked": {"count": blocked_count, "open_asks": open_asks}`), but BOTH live-line consumers key ONLY off open_asks, never off count: the tool's _work_phrase (modules/tools/discovery/handlers_fleet.py:45-52 `if entry["blocked"]["open_asks"]: return "blocked: awaiting answer"` … else `"idle"`) and its ANOMALIES blocked_with_open_ask bucket (handlers_fleet.py:98-102), and the frontend liveLine (frontend/components/agents/fleet-tab.tsx:26-34 `if (agent.blocked.open_asks.length > 0) …` else `idle`). open_asks is populated only from pending KIND_QUESTION grants (fleet_state.py:239-249 `_asks_source` filters `ApprovalGrant.kind == KIND_QUESTION`). But blocked_at is set on many NON-question paths, each of which leaves open_asks empty: a manual API block with a reason (api/board_tasks.py:549 `task.blocked_at = …` + :550 blocked_reason, no grant at all), an approval-pending block that raises a KIND_APPROVAL grant NOT a question (api/board_tasks.py:1048-1089 `_board_task_blocked_pending_approval` → status='blocked', blocked_at set, blocked_reason references the approval grant), and the mission→board bridge (services/orchestration_board_bridge.py:279,372). In every such case the task's status is 'blocked' (not in_progress → _current_from_board returns None, fleet_state.py:273-289; not 'assigned' → queue_depth 0, :368), so the agent has current=None, queue_depth=0, blocked.count>=1, open_asks=[]. Result: the fleet tab row and the platform_fleet_status per-line rendering both show 'idle', and the anomalies section flags nothing — even though platform_fleet_status's own description (actions_fleet.py:18-26) advertises answering 'is anyone stuck?'. This directly undercuts PRD-228 G3 (a real 'working/idle/blocked' line per agent) and G2 (a grounded 'how's the team doing?'). blocked.count has no assertion in test_prd228_fleet_tool.py or fleet-tab.test.tsx beyond appearing as 0 in fixtures; the realdb 'Stuck' fixture (test_prd228_fleet_state_realdb.py:130-142) happens to pair blocked_at WITH a KIND_QUESTION ask, so the open_asks-empty case is untested. FIX: make both consumers treat blocked.count>0 (with no open ask) as a blocked state distinct from idle, reusing the already-computed count (no read-model change needed — the data is already in the response).
acceptanceCriteria: The tool live-line derivation (modules/tools/discovery/handlers_fleet.py `_work_phrase`) renders an agent with blocked.count>0 as BLOCKED (not 'idle') even when open_asks is empty — e.g. 'blocked: awaiting answer' when an open ask exists, else a plain 'blocked' line — reusing the already-emitted blocked.count; and the ANOMALIES section flags such agents (a blocked bucket keyed off blocked.count, distinct from or superseding blocked_with_open_ask) so 'is anyone stuck?' catches approval-/manually-blocked agents [orchestrator/modules/tools/discovery/handlers_fleet.py] DONE — handlers_fleet.py _work_phrase now returns 'blocked: awaiting answer' when open_asks is non-empty, else a plain 'blocked' line when blocked.count>0 (both supersede working), else working/idle — reusing the already-emitted blocked.count so approval-/manually-blocked agents never read 'idle'. Anomalies gained a disjoint blocked_no_ask bucket keyed off blocked.count>0 AND open_asks==[] (distinct from blocked_with_open_ask; the union is the full 'who is stuck' set); _as_text renders 'BLOCKED (no open ask): <name> (<n> task(s) blocked)'.

The frontend liveLine (frontend/components/agents/fleet-tab.tsx) renders an agent with blocked.count>0 and no open ask as a 'blocked' line (not 'idle'), using the blocked tone, without introducing a new modal or a second hook [frontend/components/agents/fleet-tab.tsx] DONE — fleet-tab.tsx liveLine gained an `agent.blocked.count > 0` branch (below the open_asks branch, above current) returning {text:'blocked', tone:'blocked'} → the destructive tone, not idle. No new modal (still the shared AgentDetailsModal via onViewDetails) and no second hook (still useFleetState).

New tests: a fixture fleet entry with blocked.count==1 and open_asks==[] (an approval-/manually-blocked task, NOT a question) renders a 'blocked' live line (NOT 'idle') AND is flagged in the anomalies section — in the tool renderer (orchestrator/tests/test_prd228_fleet_tool.py) and in the fleet tab (frontend/components/agents/__tests__/fleet-tab.test.tsx); the existing blocked-wins and idle cases still pass [orchestrator/tests/, frontend] DONE — tool: test_blocked_without_open_ask_is_blocked_not_idle (blocked_count=1, open_asks=[], current=None → ' — blocked — ' line not 'idle'; anomalies.blocked_no_ask==['Approval']; 'BLOCKED (no open ask): Approval (1 task(s) blocked)' in text; the idle agent beside it stays ' — idle — ') + test_blocked_count_supersedes_working_line. frontend: 'a blocked agent with no open ask still shows blocked, not idle (P228-RVW-5)' asserts destructive tone + no 'idle'. Existing blocked-wins-over-working (open_asks) + idle cases still green.

userStories.title: watches/asks degradation is indistinguishable from a genuine zero — no watches_available/asks_available flag, so platform_fleet_status answers 'is anyone stuck?' with a confident false 'none' during a source failure
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (chain 5/6 adversarial re-review). P228-RVW-2 correctly made the watches/asks enrichment sources fail-soft (never 500 the route) by DEFAULTING their fields (watches → {active:0, needs_attention:0}; open_asks → []) rather than dropping the keys — a deliberate choice because the frontend contract treats them as non-optional. But unlike the COST source, which exposes cost_available + cost_source at the top level (services/fleet_state.py:421-422) precisely so a caller can tell 'unknown' from 'actually zero', the watches/asks defaults carry NO equivalent availability flag. _assemble_fleet already computes the signal locally — watches_available = watches is not None; asks_available = asks is not None (fleet_state.py:353-354) — but the response dict (fleet_state.py:417-424) emits only cost_available/cost_source and DROPS watches_available/asks_available on the floor. Scenario: a transient failure on watches or approval_grants (lock contention, replica lag, the escalation_level migration-drift class already seen in this codebase) during a GET /api/v1/fleet call makes _safe_watches/_safe_asks (fleet_state.py:222-236, 252-266) catch and return None; every agent's watches defaults to {active:0, needs_attention:0} and open_asks to [], and the response is a normal-looking 200 with no degradation marker. platform_fleet_status's ANOMALIES section (modules/tools/discovery/handlers_fleet.py:92-102) then computes over_budget_watches from needs_attention and blocked_with_open_ask from open_asks over the zeroed data and reports 'none' for both — so Auto (or a human) asking 'is anyone stuck?' or 'is anyone over budget?' during that window gets a confidently WRONG 'no', with nothing in the payload to indicate the source was down. This is the silent-zero-reads-as-truth failure class the fail-soft posture is meant to avoid (omission/observability is honest; a silent zero is a lie); the cost source already models the honest pattern. FIX: surface the already-computed watches_available/asks_available in the response (mirror cost_available) and make the degradation observable in the tool rendering, so a defaulted zero is distinguishable from a real zero. This does NOT reverse RVW-2's keep-not-drop contract — the fields stay present and shape-complete; it only adds the availability signal alongside them.
acceptanceCriteria: get_fleet_state's response carries watches_available and asks_available booleans (mirroring cost_available at services/fleet_state.py:421), set False when _safe_watches / _safe_asks returned None — reusing the watches_available/asks_available values _assemble_fleet already computes at fleet_state.py:353-354; the read-only invariant is preserved (no .add/.commit/.flush in the service) [orchestrator/services/fleet_state.py]

platform_fleet_status makes watches/asks source degradation observable rather than reporting a silent 'none' — when watches_available or asks_available is False, the compact/ANOMALIES output states the source was unavailable (e.g. a 'watches: source unavailable' / 'asks: source unavailable' notice) instead of implying a clean 'no anomalies' [orchestrator/modules/tools/discovery/handlers_fleet.py]

The frontend FleetStateResponse contract (frontend/lib/api-client.ts) carries watches_available/asks_available; the fleet tab does not misreport a degraded source as clean (a minimal indicator is acceptable — no new modal, no second hook) [frontend/lib/api-client.ts, frontend/components/agents/fleet-tab.tsx]

New tests: monkeypatch _watches_source (and separately _asks_source) to raise → get_fleet_state returns watches_available:false (resp. asks_available:false) while still 200-shaped with every agent present (extend tests/test_prd228_fleet_state.py); platform_fleet_status surfaces the degradation notice rather than 'none' (tests/test_prd228_fleet_tool.py) [orchestrator/tests/]
